summary: This is a foundational library file that sets up shared utilities for a family of AI-powered shell commands. It provides reusable helpers for communicating with Ollama (a local AI model), processing output, collecting user input interactively, and dispatching commands through a menu system. The file is designed to load first (via the leading underscore in its filename) so that all the ai-* functions that depend on it have these utilities available.

explanations.18: This creates a global associative array (like a dictionary or hash map) called AI_COMMANDS that will store the names and descriptions of all available ai-* functions that register themselves.
explanations.19: Similar to line 18, this creates a global associative array AI_PARAMS to track what kind of user input each command needs (file picker, language selector, etc.).
explanations.28: This gets the Ollama server address from an environment variable if set, otherwise defaults to the local machine on port 11434.
explanations.29: The curl command attempts to reach the Ollama server's /api/tags endpoint with a 2-second timeout; if it fails, the function returns an error code.
explanations.49: The 'print -r --' command outputs the prompt exactly as-is without interpreting special characters, and the '--' tells it to stop processing options.
explanations.50: This pipes the prompt into jq, which reads it as raw text (-R), combines it all into a single string (-s), and then wraps it in a JSON object with the model name and stream setting.
explanations.69: The [[ ]] is a bash conditional; the '*' acts as a wildcard, so this checks if the text contains any backticks (which would indicate Markdown code fences).
explanations.74: The awk script toggles a boolean variable 'inside' each time it sees a line starting with triple backticks, and prints lines only when inside is true—effectively extracting only the code between fences.
explanations.86: The 'command -v' built-in checks if a program is available on the system by searching the PATH; the output is sent to /dev/null so we only care about the exit code.
explanations.98: The :A syntax expands the path to an absolute path (resolving any relative path components like '..' or symlinks).
explanations.99: The ${variable#pattern} syntax removes the pattern from the start of the variable; here it strips off the current working directory prefix to leave only the relative path.
explanations.107: This uses a glob pattern [yY]* to match the answer against 'y' or 'Y' followed by anything; the [[ ]] returns 0 (success) if it matches, 1 otherwise.
explanations.134: The output of the 'git diff --staged' command is stored in the variable 'diff' for later inspection and manipulation.
explanations.143: The (( )) syntax evaluates arithmetic expressions; ${#diff} gets the string length, so this checks if the diff size is within the acceptable limit.
explanations.151: The $() syntax runs a command and substitutes its output; here git diff --stat is being captured into the summary variable.
explanations.158: The ${variable[1,$max]} syntax extracts a substring from position 1 to position $max, truncating the summary to the character limit.
explanations.172: This attempts to find the bat command and stores its name in bat_bin; the '&&' means the next part only runs if the command-v check succeeds.
explanations.173: The variable preview is being reassigned to use bat (with syntax highlighting) if available, falling back to plain cat if bat errors out.
explanations.238: The ${+variable} syntax checks whether a variable exists (returns 1 if it does, 0 if it doesn't); this checks if the command name is registered in AI_COMMANDS.
explanations.250: The ${(ok)array} syntax iterates over array keys in sorted order; the 'o' means sorted, 'k' means keys only.
explanations.269: The ${(s: :)string} syntax splits a string on spaces into an array; here it's splitting the AI_PARAMS value (like 'file language') into individual parameter types.
explanations.284: The [[ -n "$n" ]] checks if the variable n is non-empty; this only adds it to args if the user actually entered a number (not just hit Enter for the default).
